title: C/C++ Build Pipeline Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on how C/C++ source becomes a program: preprocessor, compile and link stages, header guards, ODR, inline/static, linker errors, libraries, CMake and compiler flags.

chapters.title: Build Pipeline Mental Model
points: Four stages: preprocess (.cpp → translation unit) → compile (→ .o object file) → assemble → link (objects + libs → executable)
Each .cpp is compiled independently into its own translation unit (TU); only the linker sees across TUs
Inspect each stage: g++ -E (preprocessed output), -S (assembly), -c (object file only), no flag (full link)
Declaration says a name exists (compile needs it); definition provides the body or storage (link needs it)
Compile errors = syntax/type problems in one TU; linker errors = missing or duplicate symbols across TUs

chapters.title: Preprocessor and Header Guards
points: Preprocessor does pure text substitution before compilation: #include pastes file contents, #define replaces tokens, #if/#ifdef selects code
Header guard: #ifndef FOO_H / #define FOO_H / ... / #endif prevents the same header being pasted twice into one TU
#pragma once is the shorter non-standard-but-universal alternative; guards are fully standard and survive copied or symlinked files
Function-like macros do not evaluate safely: #define SQ(x) x*x gives SQ(1+2)=5; parenthesize args or use constexpr/inline functions
Use #include <...> for system/library paths and "..." for project files; -I adds search directories; -D NAME=1 defines a macro from the command line

chapters.title: ODR, inline and static
points: One Definition Rule: a non-inline function or variable may be defined exactly once in the whole program; violating it gives multiple definition errors or silent UB
Never define a normal function or global variable in a header: each including TU gets its own copy and the linker reports duplicates
inline (functions and C++17 variables) allows identical definitions in many TUs, so the linker keeps one; it is about linkage, not a speed hint
static at namespace scope gives internal linkage: every TU gets a private copy, invisible to the linker; an anonymous namespace does the same
extern int x; declares without defining; put exactly one int x = 0; in one .cpp. Classes, templates and constexpr functions are implicitly ODR-safe in headers

chapters.title: Linker Errors and Libraries
points: undefined reference to 'foo()': declared but never defined, or the defining .o/library was not passed to the linker; check the signature and namespace match exactly
multiple definition of 'foo': defined in a header without inline, or the same .cpp is linked twice
Link order matters for static libs: put libraries after the objects that need them, e.g. g++ main.o -lfoo; -L adds a library dir, -lfoo finds libfoo.a/.so
Static library (.a, built with ar rcs): copied into the executable, so it is self-contained, larger, and needs relinking to update

Shared library (.so/.dll): loaded at run time, so it is smaller and updatable, but needs -fPIC when building, and a missing one gives a cannot open shared object file error (check LD_LIBRARY_PATH or rpath)

chapters.title: CMake and Compiler Flags
points: CMake generates build files (Make/Ninja); it does not compile itself. Workflow: cmake -S . -B build, then cmake --build build
Minimal CMakeLists.txt: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20), project(app CXX), add_executable(app main.cpp util.cpp)
Targets carry properties: add_library(foo STATIC foo.cpp), target_include_directories(foo PUBLIC include), target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE foo)
PUBLIC propagates to consumers, PRIVATE is internal only, INTERFACE is consumers only; set the standard with set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20) and CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE (Debug/Release)
Warnings and build-type flags: -Wall -Wextra -Werror, -std=c++20, -g debug info, -O0 vs -O2 optimization, -fsanitize=address,undefined to catch bugs at run time

chapters.title: Build Cheat Sheet
points: Stage flags: g++ -E preprocess, -S assembly, -c object, plain = full build and link
Header safety: always add #ifndef guard or #pragma once; never define non-inline functions or globals in headers
Linker triage: undefined reference = missing definition or library; multiple definition = header definition without inline or duplicate source
Library commands: ar rcs libfoo.a foo.o; g++ -shared -fPIC foo.cpp -o libfoo.so; link with -L. -lfoo
CMake loop: cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build; start warnings with -Wall -Wextra
